brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor mapping chromatic notes to color swatches creates a memorable, distinctive premise that justifies the layout
Clear three-panel architecture with confident gradient title and consistent dark surface gives immediate orientation
Swatch row reads instantly as both a keyboard and a palette, fusing the two domains visually
dominant_weaknesses: Right Color Palette panel is clipped off-canvas and Export buttons truncate text — a fundamental layout/overflow failure
Swatch colors are arbitrary rainbow rather than a derived harmony — the 'C-E-G chord' shows no visual locking relationship between picked notes
Spacing is inconsistent: huge empty middle, cramped left controls, oversized waveform card floating without anchor or purpose
fix_priorities: Fix right-panel clipping and button truncation; constrain layout to viewport with proper grid
Make swatch colors algorithmically derived from harmony type so chord selection visibly locks related hues
Tighten vertical rhythm — reduce dead space around chord card and integrate waveform meaningfully (e.g., tied to tempo)
Unify swatch palette into a coherent tonal system rather than 12 unrelated saturations
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral appeal from the gradient title and colorful keys outpaces behavioral clarity (truncated controls, unclear chord-to-color mapping) while the reflective concept remains the strongest layer.
rationale.intent_fit: The metaphor is present and intriguing, but the colors don't actually 'lock like chords' — harmony selection produces no visible relational change, so the brief is illustrated more than executed.
